title: Synapse counts increased first-arrival rank agreement between models of two selected adult worm maps
abstract: We tested whether synapse-count weights support repeatable source orders of mean first-arrival times in a random-walk model. Two adult C. elegans chemical maps gave a fixed 154-cell core. The mean within-target rank correlation between maps was 0.7677 with counts and 0.7154 with binary weights. Counts improved agreement for 112 of 154 targets. The observed score exceeded all 999 draws under each of two count shuffles, one within sources and one within targets, with supports fixed. Square-root and capped counts retained a mean advantage over binary weights. On the common support, binary models agreed perfectly by construction and count models agreed at 0.9105, so counts did not improve agreement for every support choice. Independent absorbing solves reproduced all primary ranks. Two animals, a panel selected from both maps, simplified positive transitions and no matched activity limit the result to this model benchmark. Original code, aggregate draws, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Synapse-count weights increased mean source-rank agreement over binary weights in two selected adult models. Count placement exceeded two fixed-support shuffle references. Shared-support binary models agree by construction.
